title: Decide what to do with six suspicious emails reported to the help desk
situation: Six emails came in this morning and several staff reported them. One claims to be from a Microsoft-like domain asking for a password. Another uses an executive's name from a Gmail address to ask for an urgent wire transfer. Others include an invoice with a disguised program attached and a fake mailbox warning sent from our own domain. Headers can lie, so every sender check must be redone, not trusted.
your_task: Re-check each email's SPF, DKIM and DMARC results yourself instead of trusting the headers.
Look for warning signs: look-alike domains, mismatched links, pressure language and dangerous attachments.
Score each message and decide to deliver, quarantine or reject it.
Label each threat type so the help desk can warn staff.
why_it_matters: Email is the most common way attackers get in. One fake payment request or stolen password can cost the company money or hand an attacker a working account.
done_when: 2 emails are delivered, 3 are quarantined and 1 is rejected.
Each bad email is labeled: credential phishing, business email compromise, malware delivery or domain spoofing.
The forged 'pass' result in the spoofed message's header is called out.
Each verdict lists the warning signs that drove its score.

glossary.Sender Policy Framework (SPF): A list a domain publishes of the servers allowed to send its email.
glossary.DomainKeys Identified Mail (DKIM): A digital signature that proves an email came from the domain and was not changed.
glossary.DMARC (Domain-based Message Authenticati: A domain's rule for what to do with mail that fails SPF and DKIM checks.
glossary.Alignment: Whether the domain that passed SPF or DKIM matches the domain shown in the From line.
glossary.Business email compromise (BEC): A scam where someone pretends to be a boss or vendor to get money sent.
glossary.Typosquatting: Registering a look-alike domain, such as replacing an 'o' with a zero, to fool people.
glossary.Quarantine: Holding an email aside so nobody can open it until it is reviewed.

talking_point: Recomputed SPF, DKIM and DMARC for 6 reported emails and quarantined or rejected 4 threats (credential phishing, CEO wire-fraud impersonation, a disguised executable and a spoofed company domain), while delivering the 2 legitimate messages.
